'''Thérèse Anne Coffey, Baroness Coffey'''{{efn|name=diacritics}}  (born 18 November 1971) is a British politician who served as [[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] from September to October 2022 under [[Liz Truss]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liz Truss – live updates: Truss outlines three priorities as PM – as Raab and Shapps confirm departure |url=https://news.sky.com/story/liz-truss-prime-minister-live-updates-picks-cabinet-boris-johnson-12593360 |access-date=6 September 2022 |website=[[Sky News]] |language=en |archive-date=6 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906062334/https://news.sky.com/story/liz-truss-prime-minister-live-updates-picks-cabinet-boris-johnson-12593360 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A member of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]], she was the first female [[deputy prime minister]] in [[British history]]. Coffey served as [[Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|Environment Secretary]], [[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]], and [[Work and Pensions Secretary]] while serving as the [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|member of Parliament]] (MP) for [[Suffolk Coastal (UK Parliament constituency)|Suffolk Coastal]] from 2010 to 2024. Since 2025, she has been a Member of the [[House of Lords]] as a [[life peer]].

Coffey served under Prime Minister [[Theresa May]] as a [[Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State|parliamentary under-secretary of state]] at the [[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs]] from 2016 to 2019, before serving under Prime Minister [[Boris Johnson]] as a [[Minister of State|minister of state]] at the same department from July to September 2019. In September 2019, after [[Amber Rudd]] resigned from Johnson's [[Cabinet of the United Kingdom|cabinet]], Coffey was appointed as secretary of state for work and pensions.

After Johnson resigned in 2022, Coffey supported [[Liz Truss]]'s bid to become Conservative leader. Following Truss's appointment as prime minister in September 2022, Coffey was appointed deputy prime minister and secretary of state for health and social care. After Truss resigned in October 2022, Coffey was appointed by [[Rishi Sunak]] as secretary of state for environment, food and rural affairs. After [[November 2023 British cabinet reshuffle|resigning in November 2023]], Coffey lost her seat in Parliament at the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]]<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=2024-07-05 |title=Key moments from a dramatic election night |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4ng3vz5gdno |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> but was appointed to the [[House of Lords]] later that year.

==Education and early life==
Thérèse Coffey was born on 18 November 1971<ref name="WW" /> in [[Billinge Hospital]] in [[Wigan]], [[Lancashire]], to Tom Coffey and Alice George and grew up in Liverpool. She went to [[St Mary's College, Crosby]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrated Alumni |url=https://stmarys.ac/celebrated-alumni |website=St Marys College |access-date=29 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112134757/https://stmarys.ac/celebrated-alumni |archive-date=12 January 2019}}</ref><ref>[http://www.friendsofstmarys.com/my-decade/1980s/1980s-articles/168-1968-university-places-offered.html ''Crosby Herald'' 16 February 1989] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425063838/http://www.friendsofstmarys.com/my-decade/1980s/1980s-articles/168-1968-university-places-offered.html |date=25 April 2012 }} from ''Friends of St. Mary's'' website</ref> and [[St Edward's College]], [[Liverpool]].<ref name="WW">{{Who's Who |author=Anon|title=Coffey, Dr Therese Anne |id=U251482 |year=2011 |edition=online [[Oxford University Press]] |location=Oxford|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U251482}}</ref> Coffey then briefly attended the [[University of Oxford]] as an undergraduate student of [[Somerville College, Oxford]] in 1989 to study chemistry.<ref>{{cite web |date=20 July 2016 |title=Four Somervillian MPs appointed to new roles in Cabinet reshuffle |url=https://www.some.ox.ac.uk/news/four-somervillian-mps-appointed-to-new-roles-in-cabinet-reshuffle/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114154616/https://www.some.ox.ac.uk/news/four-somervillian-mps-appointed-to-new-roles-in-cabinet-reshuffle/ |archive-date=14 January 2021 |accessdate=10 October 2021 |work=Somerville, University of Oxford}}</ref><ref name="Tip for chief whip">{{cite news |last1=Ivers |first1=Charlotte |title=Thérèse Coffey: the cigar-smoking, karaoke-singing tip for chief whip |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/therese-coffey-the-cigar-smoking-karaoke-singing-tip-for-chief-whip-m339pspw6 |access-date=20 August 2022 |work=The Sunday Times |date=20 August 2022 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=20 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820180242/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/therese-coffey-the-cigar-smoking-karaoke-singing-tip-for-chief-whip-m339pspw6 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, in 1991 she was asked to withdraw having obtained poor college examination results twice allegedly due to spending too much time on extracurricular activities including rowing and politics.<ref name="guardian-20220907">{{Cite news |last=Ben |first=Quinn |date=7 September 2022 |title=Thérèse Coffey had to leave Oxford University – but made it to deputy PM |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/sep/07/therese-coffey-had-to-leave-oxford-university-but-made-it-to-deputy-pm |access-date=7 September 2022 |archive-date=7 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220907180732/https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/sep/07/therese-coffey-had-to-leave-oxford-university-but-made-it-to-deputy-pm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Coffey then attended [[University College London]], where she obtained a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree (with [[upper second class honours]]) in chemistry in 1993<ref>[https://www.ucl.ac.uk/chemistry/sites/chemistry/files/2011-newsletter.pdf UCL Chemistry Newsletter 2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005120843/https://www.ucl.ac.uk/chemistry/sites/chemistry/files/2011-newsletter.pdf |date=5 October 2022 }} - website of [[University College London]]</ref> and later a [[PhD]] in chemistry in 1998.<ref name="tphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |publisher=University College London (University of London) |title=Structural and reactivity studies of Bis(imido) complexes of molybdenum |first=Therese Anne |last=Coffey |date=1998 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1759292059|website=proquest.com|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.286225}} |oclc=557362689}}</ref><ref name="guardian-20220907" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thisiskent.co.uk/euroelections/Conservative-Party-candidates-Euro-elections/article-992885-detail/article.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120913140614/http://www.thisiskent.co.uk/euroelections/Conservative-Party-candidates-Euro-elections/article-992885-detail/article.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 September 2012 |title=Biodata on Coffey}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating Coffey worked in a number of roles for [[Mars Incorporated]], including as finance director for [[Mars, Incorporated#Mars Drinks UK|Mars Drinks UK]]. She then worked for the [[BBC]] as a property finance manager.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.lsesu.com/ents/event/2613/ | title=Q&A Session with DR Thérèse Coffey MP | work=London School of Economics Student Union | accessdate=10 October 2021 | archive-date=10 October 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010150652/https://www.lsesu.com/ents/event/2613/ | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.politics.co.uk/reference/therese-coffey/ | title=Coffey, Therese | work=politics.co.uk | accessdate=10 October 2021 | archive-date=12 March 2022 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210907/https://www.politics.co.uk/reference/therese-coffey/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

===Political career===
In the [[2004 European Parliament election in the United Kingdom|European Parliament elections in June 2004]], Coffey stood for election to the [[European Parliament]] for [[South East England (European Parliament constituency)|South East England]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2004 Election Candidates |url=http://www.europarl.europa.eu/unitedkingdom/en/your-meps/european_elections/previous_election_results/10-june-2004/2004_election_candidates.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813143504/http://www.europarl.europa.eu/unitedkingdom/en/your-meps/european_elections/previous_election_results/10-june-2004/2004_election_candidates.html |archive-date=13 August 2018 |access-date=13 August 2018 |work=European Parliament Liaison Office}}</ref> The Conservative Party won 35.2% of the vote, giving it four seats, but Coffey was seventh on the list in this [[proportional representation]] system, and was not elected.<ref>{{cite web |title=2004 Election candidates |url=http://www.europarl.org.uk/section/2004/2004-election-candidates |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091004091828/http://www.europarl.org.uk/section/2004/2004-election-candidates |archive-date=4 October 2009 |access-date=4 June 2009 |work=UK Office of the European Parliament |df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=South East |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/politics/eu-regions/E15000008 |access-date=31 May 2016 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

Coffey stood as the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] candidate for [[Wrexham (UK Parliament constituency)|Wrexham]] at the [[2005 United Kingdom general election|2005 general election]], coming third with 20% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/person/9417/therese-coffey |work=The Guardian |title=Politics section Therese Coffey: Electoral history and profile |access-date=16 December 2016 |archive-date=3 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703124627/https://www.theguardian.com/politics |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="electoralcalculus2005">{{cite web |title=Election Data 2005 |url=http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2005ob.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111015054249/http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2005ob.txt |archive-date=15 October 2011 |access-date=18 October 2015 |publisher=[[Electoral Calculus]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=2005-05-05 |title=Wrexham: Constituency > Politics > guardian.co.uk |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/constituency/1457/wrexham |access-date=2011-01-22 |work=Election 2010 |publisher=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Wrexham parliamentary constituency - Election 2005 |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/shared/vote2005/html/652.stm |via=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref>

At the [[2009 European Parliament election in the United Kingdom|2009 European Parliament elections]], Coffey missed out by one place on being elected to the European Parliament for South East England.<ref>{{cite web |title=South East Region – Statement of Parties and Individual Candidates Nominated and Notice of Poll |url=http://www.reading.gov.uk/Documents/Council_and_Democracy/Electoral/NoticeOfPoll.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090611233231/http://www.reading.gov.uk/Documents/Council_and_Democracy/Electoral/NoticeOfPoll.pdf |archive-date=11 June 2009 |access-date=15 March 2018 |publisher=Government of the United Kingdom |df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=European Election 2009 – UK Results – South East |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/shared/bsp/hi/elections/euro/09/html/ukregion_35.stm |access-date=15 March 2018 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> The Conservative Party won 34.79% of the vote, giving it four seats, and placing her fifth on the party list.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/eu/5291332/European-elections-2009-South-East-region.html |title=European elections 2009: South East region |date=26 May 2009 |website=telegraph.co.uk |access-date=2 April 2018 |archive-date=12 March 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210946/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/eu/5291332/European-elections-2009-South-East-region.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Parliamentary career==
At the [[2010 United Kingdom general election|2010 general election]], Coffey was elected as MP for [[Suffolk Coastal (UK Parliament constituency)|Suffolk Coastal]] with 46.4% of the vote and a majority of 9,128.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/shared/election2010/results/constituency/e56.stm |title=BBC News – Election 2010 – Constituency – Suffolk Coastal |website=news.bbc.co.uk |access-date=14 January 2019 |archive-date=12 March 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210946/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/shared/election2010/results/constituency/e56.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="electoralcalculus2010">{{cite web |title=Election Data 2010 |url=http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2010.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130726162034/http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2010.txt |archive-date=26 July 2013 |access-date=17 October 2015 |publisher=[[Electoral Calculus]]}}</ref> She is a supporter of the Free Enterprise Group.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.freeenterprise.org.uk/|title=Free Enterprise Group | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111111133857/http://www.freeenterprise.org.uk/ | archive-date=11 November 2011 }}</ref>

On 6 July 2011, Coffey defended [[Rebekah Brooks]] over the ''[[News of the World]]''{{'}}s involvement in the [[news media phone hacking scandal]]. She said a "[[witch hunt]]" was developing against Brooks, and that simply to say Brooks was editor of the newspaper at the time was not enough evidence against her. Coffey became a member of the [[Culture, Media and Sport Select Committee]] inquiry into the hacking scandal in 2012. In that committee, she declined to support any motions critical of [[Rupert Murdoch|Rupert]] and [[James Murdoch]].<ref>''The Guardian''. 2 May 2012.</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Prodhan |first1=Georgina |title=UK Conservatives tried to soften Murdoch criticism |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/newscorp-hacking-split-idINL5E8G1AX720120501 |work=Reuters |date=1 May 2012 |language=en |access-date=6 September 2022 |archive-date=6 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906211055/https://www.reuters.com/article/newscorp-hacking-split-idINL5E8G1AX720120501 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, she later joined the majority of her party in voting for [[exemplary damages]] to be a default consequence to deter press misbehaviour.<ref>[http://www.publicwhip.org.uk/division.php?date=2013-03-18&number=192&mpn=Therese_Coffey&mpc=Suffolk_Coastal&house=commons The Public Whip] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714120952/http://www.publicwhip.org.uk/division.php?date=2013-03-18&number=192&mpn=Therese_Coffey&mpc=Suffolk_Coastal&house=commons |date=14 July 2014 }} Retrieved 26 March 2013</ref>

=== Early frontbench career ===
After serving as a member of the [[Culture, Media and Sport Committee]] from July 2010 to October 2012, Coffey was appointed [[Parliamentary Private Secretary]] to [[Michael Fallon]], Minister for Business and Energy.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.uk/biographies/commons/dr-therese-coffey/4098 |title=Dr Thérèse Coffey MP |website=UK Parliament |access-date=2 July 2016 |archive-date=22 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822194300/http://www.parliament.uk/biographies/commons/dr-therese-coffey/4098 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Coffey faced criticism in 2011 from some Suffolk residents over her support for the government's proposal to sell off forestry and woodland in public ownership. Protesters argued that "experience shows us that when private landowners come in they close car parks and make access as difficult as possible".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Robinson |first1=Craig |date=12 February 2011 |title=Gallery: MP faces criticism at heated forest meeting |url=http://www.eadt.co.uk/news/gallery_mp_faces_criticism_at_heated_forest_meeting_1_800226 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714213110/http://www.eadt.co.uk/news/gallery_mp_faces_criticism_at_heated_forest_meeting_1_800226 |archive-date=14 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014 |work=East Anglian Daily Times}}</ref> The government later dropped the proposal in January 2013.<ref>{{cite news |date=31 January 2013 |title='No sell-off' for public forests |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-21275432 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720002158/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-21275432 |archive-date=20 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

Coffey's decision to write a paper for the Free Enterprise Group recommending pensioners should pay [[National Insurance]] contributions on earnings provoked criticism among some older constituents, who claimed that in an already tough economic environment, it was wrong to tax pensioners further. Coffey said that she had "no regrets writing about National Insurance" and that it was "a policy proposal – it is by no means, at this stage, anymore than that".<ref name="EADT pensioners">{{cite web |last1=Porrit |first1=Richard |date=16 July 2012 |title=Suffolk Coastal: MP stands by proposals to force pensioners to pay NI |url=http://www.eadt.co.uk/news/suffolk_coastal_mp_stands_by_proposals_to_force_pensioners_to_pay_ni_1_1446701 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714145136/http://www.eadt.co.uk/news/suffolk_coastal_mp_stands_by_proposals_to_force_pensioners_to_pay_ni_1_1446701 |archive-date=14 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014 |work=East Anglian Daily Times}}</ref>

In February 2013, Coffey voted against the legalisation of [[same-sex marriage]], stating: "I shall be voting against the Bill because my perspective on what marriage is really about is different from that of some other Members... for me it is fundamentally still about family, the bedrock of society."<ref>[[Hansard]], Commons Debates, col 220, 5 February 2013.</ref> She again voted against same-sex marriage in 2019 when Parliament considered the same question for Northern Ireland.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theyworkforyou.com/mp/24771/therese_coffey/suffolk_coastal/divisions?policy=6686 |title=Therese Coffey MP, Suffolk Coastal |work=TheyWorkForYou |publisher=mySociety |access-date=11 September 2019 |archive-date=20 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191220143353/https://www.theyworkforyou.com/mp/24771/therese_coffey/suffolk_coastal/divisions?policy=6686 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-49657071 |title=Liz Truss given ministerial role covering equalities and women's issues |work=BBC News |date=10 September 2019 |access-date=11 September 2019 |archive-date=12 March 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210923/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-49657071 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2014, she was appointed an [[Whip (politics)|assistant government whip]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Thérèse Coffey |url=https://www.conservatives.com/OurTeam/Members-of-Parliament/Coffey-Therese |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525021646/https://www.conservatives.com/OurTeam/Members-of-Parliament/Coffey-Therese |archive-date=25 May 2019 |access-date=2 July 2016 |website=www.conservatives.com}}</ref>

At the [[2015 United Kingdom general election|2015 general election]], Coffey was re-elected as MP for Suffolk Coastal with an increased vote share of 51.9% and an increased majority of 18,842.<ref name="electoralcalculus">{{cite web |title=Election Data 2015 |url=http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2015.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151017112223/http://www.electoralcalculus.co.uk/electdata_2015.txt |archive-date=17 October 2015 |access-date=17 October 2015 |publisher=[[Electoral Calculus]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=2015 Election Results |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/politics/constituencies/E14000981 |access-date=8 May 2015 |website=BBC News}}</ref> After the election, she was appointed [[Deputy Leader of the House of Commons]] on 11 May 2015.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/people/therese-coffey |title=Thérèse Coffey MP |work=GOV.UK |access-date=2 July 2016 |archive-date=12 March 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210928/https://www.gov.uk/government/people/therese-coffey |url-status=live}}</ref>

In October 2016, Coffey was criticised by the then [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] leader [[Tim Farron]] for accepting hospitality worth £890 from [[Ladbrokes]] after supporting the gambling industry in parliament as part of the Culture, Media and Sport Committee;  she denied that she had been "influenced in her considerations on matters of related policy by any hospitality received".<ref>{{cite news |last=Lo |first=Joseph |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlo/tory-mp-criticised-after-accepting-trips-to-horse-racing-fro |title=Tory MP Criticised After Accepting Trips To Horse Racing From Ladbrokes |work=Buzzfeed |date=27 October 2016 |access-date=28 December 2017 |archive-date=29 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229112213/https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlo/tory-mp-criticised-after-accepting-trips-to-horse-racing-fro |url-status=live }}</ref>

Coffey voted in favour of a [[2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum|UK referendum on EU membership]] and consistently voted to proceed with the [[Brexit]] process,<ref>[https://www.theresecoffey.co.uk/brexit-updates Brexit Updates]. Therese Coffey. Retrieved 21 November 2022.</ref> although she backed the Remain campaign during the referendum.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/21593923.mp-branded-traitor-many-times-eu/|title=MP branded a 'traitor' many times over the EU|last=Geater|first=Paul|date=21 June 2016|work=[[East Anglian Daily Times]]|access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref>

At the snap [[2017 United Kingdom general election|2017 general election]], Coffey was again re-elected, with an increased vote share of 58.1% and a decreased majority of 16,012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archived copy |url=http://www.eastsuffolk.gov.uk/assets/Elections/Election-notices-WDC/2017/Parliamentary-General-Election/Statement-of-Persons-Nominated-Notice-of-Poll-Suffolk-Coastal-Constituency.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519012451/http://www.eastsuffolk.gov.uk/assets/Elections/Election-notices-WDC/2017/Parliamentary-General-Election/Statement-of-Persons-Nominated-Notice-of-Poll-Suffolk-Coastal-Constituency.pdf |archive-date=19 May 2017 |access-date=11 May 2017}}</ref>

In the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] she sat on the [[Environmental Audit Committee]] from September 2017 to November 2019, ex-officio due to her ministerial role.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr Thérèse Coffey – Parliamentary career |url=https://members.parliament.uk/member/4098/career |website=UK Parliament |access-date=22 June 2022 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122123600/https://members.parliament.uk/member/4098/career |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Thérèse Coffey with Kitack Lim - 2017 (36004153375).jpg|left|thumb|Coffey with [[Kitack Lim]] in 2017]]

=== Secretary of State for Work and Pensions ===
Following the resignation of [[Amber Rudd]] in September 2019, Coffey joined the Cabinet as [[Secretary of State for Work and Pensions]]. She retained her position in Prime Minister [[Boris Johnson]]'s [[2020 British cabinet reshuffle|February 2020 cabinet reshuffle]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Proctor |first1=Kate |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2020/feb/12/cabinet-reshuffle-expected-winners-and-losers-johnson |title=Cabinet reshuffle: expected winners and losers in Johnson's new order |date=12 February 2020 |work=The Guardian |access-date=1 March 2020 |last2=Mason |first2=Rowena |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=12 March 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220312210931/https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2020/feb/12/cabinet-reshuffle-expected-winners-and-losers-johnson |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-49043973|title=Cabinet reshuffle: Who is in Boris Johnson's new cabinet?|date=14 February 2020|work=BBC News|access-date=1 March 2020|language=en-GB|archive-date=25 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725194313/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-49043973|url-status=live}}</ref>

Coffey was again re-elected at the [[2019 United Kingdom general election|2019 general election]], with a decreased vote share of 56.5% and an increased majority of 20,533.<ref>{{cite news |title=Suffolk Coastal Parliamentary constituency |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/politics/constituencies/E14000981 |access-date=19 November 2019 |website=BBC News |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In June 2020, Coffey responded to [[Marcus Rashford]]'s campaign for free school meals for children during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], which included a tweet from Rashford urging the government to remember Britain's poorest families. One of his tweets read, in part: "When you wake up this morning and run your shower, take a second to think about parents who have had their water turned off during lockdown." Coffey's response to his campaign was, "Water cannot be disconnected though", which he considered dismissive.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 June 2020 |title=Marcus Rashford slams Therese Coffey over tweet on water supply amid free school meals campaign |url=https://www.politicshome.com/news/article/marcus-rashford-slams-therese-coffey-over-tweet-on-water-supply-amid-free-school-meals-campaign |access-date=16 June 2020 |website=politicshome.com |last=Johnston |first=John |archive-date=16 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616214923/https://www.politicshome.com/news/article/marcus-rashford-slams-therese-coffey-over-tweet-on-water-supply-amid-free-school-meals-campaign |url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2021, Coffey was accused by opponents of miscalculating the amount of work a [[Universal Credit]] claimant would need to do in order to make up for the proposed end of the £20-a-week increase in benefits, brought in to assist people during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Speaking to ''[[BBC Breakfast]]'', Coffey said: "We're conscious that £20 a week is about two hours' extra work every week – we will be seeing what we can do to help people perhaps secure those extra hours, but ideally also to make sure they're also in a place to get better paid jobs, as well."<ref>{{cite news |date=13 September 2021 |title=Thérèse Coffey accused of getting universal credit figures wrong |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2021/sep/13/therese-coffey-accused-of-getting-universal-credit-figures-wrong |access-date=13 September 2021 |work=The Guardian |last=Walker |first=Peter |archive-date=13 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210913120048/https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2021/sep/13/therese-coffey-accused-of-getting-universal-credit-figures-wrong |url-status=live}}</ref> However, given Universal Credit's "taper rate" of 63%,<ref>{{cite web |title=Universal Credit work allowances |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/universal-credit-work-allowances/universal-credit-work-allowances |access-date=13 September 2021 |work=GOV.UK |archive-date=13 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210913134005/https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/universal-credit-work-allowances/universal-credit-work-allowances |url-status=live}}</ref> a Universal Credit claimant sees their credit reduced by 63p for every pound they generate from work.

In January 2022, Coffey tweeted support for Boris Johnson in regard to [[Partygate]] allegations, stating that she considered his apology to be sincere.<ref>{{cite news |last=Williams |first=Angus |date=13 January 2022 |title=Suffolk MP backs prime minister's 'sincere' apology over BYOB event |url=https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/therese-coffey-tweets-support-for-boris-johnson-8618544 |work=East Anglian Daily Times |access-date=6 February 2022 |archive-date=29 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220129034207/https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/therese-coffey-tweets-support-for-boris-johnson-8618544 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2022, Coffey said that, as a practising Catholic, she opposed abortion but did not condemn those who have an abortion.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cabinet minister Therese Coffey says she would 'prefer that people didn't have abortions' but law won't change |url=https://news.sky.com/story/cabinet-minister-therese-coffey-says-she-would-prefer-that-people-didnt-have-abortions-but-law-wont-change-12643326 |access-date=6 September 2022 |work=[[Sky News]] |date=30 June 2022 |archive-date=6 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906225224/https://news.sky.com/story/cabinet-minister-therese-coffey-says-she-would-prefer-that-people-didnt-have-abortions-but-law-wont-change-12643326 |url-status=live }}</ref> She had previously tabled a [[Motion (parliamentary procedure)|motion]] in 2010 calling for mental health assessments for those seeking abortion, and she also voted against [[Abortion in Northern Ireland|extending abortion rights to people in Northern Ireland]].<ref name="Wells">{{cite news |last1=Wells |first1=Ione |title=Therese Coffey's views on abortion concerning, charity says |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-62805268 |access-date=6 September 2022 |work=BBC News |date=6 September 2022 |archive-date=6 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906203201/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-62805268 |url-status=live }}</ref> Her views on abortion were criticised by Clare Murphy, CEO of the [[British Pregnancy Advisory Service]].<ref name="Wells" />

Coffey continued to defend Johnson in July 2022 when he was accused of overlooking MP [[Chris Pincher]]'s alleged sexual misconduct when he was appointed Deputy Chief Whip. Coffey went on record to say that Johnson was "not aware" of "specific" allegations relating to Pincher. She went on to say in several interviews that she felt Johnson had dealt with the issue decisively.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/politics/boris-johnson-not-aware-of-specific-chris-pincher-allegations-says-therese-coffey-3754314 |title=Boris Johnson 'not aware' of 'specific' Chris Pincher allegations, says Therese Coffey |date=3 July 2022 |access-date=3 July 2022 |work=The Scotsman |last=Brown |first=Hannah |archive-date=3 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703124629/https://www.scotsman.com/news/politics/boris-johnson-not-aware-of-specific-chris-pincher-allegations-says-therese-coffey-3754314 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Coffey was campaign manager for [[Liz Truss]] in the parliamentary stages of the [[July–September 2022 Conservative Party leadership election]], and she remained in a campaign role in the members' vote stage of the election.<ref name="Tip for chief whip"/>

=== Deputy prime minister and health secretary ===

Truss appointed Coffey as [[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|deputy prime minister]] and [[Health and Social Care Secretary|health and social care secretary]] in [[Truss ministry|her new government]] on 6 September 2022. Her appointment made her the first woman to serve as deputy prime minister.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Salisbury |first1=Josh |title=Thérèse Coffey, Kwasi Kwarteng and James Cleverly given key roles in Cabinet |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/therese-coffey-health-secretary-liz-truss-s-new-cabinet-b1023622.html |access-date=6 September 2022 |work=Evening Standard |date=6 September 2022 |language=en |archive-date=6 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906191605/https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/therese-coffey-health-secretary-liz-truss-s-new-cabinet-b1023622.html |url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2022, Coffey identified four priorities for the Department of Health "A, B, C, D" – ambulances, backlog, care, and doctors and dentists.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 September 2022 |title=Thérèse Coffey defends Truss against 'cabinet of chums' charge |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/sep/07/therese-coffey-defends-truss-against-cabinet-of-chums-charge |access-date=13 October 2022 |work=The Guardian |archive-date=13 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221013095832/https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/sep/07/therese-coffey-defends-truss-against-cabinet-of-chums-charge |url-status=live}}</ref>

Asked about nurses leaving to go abroad, Coffey said: "It is their choice of course if they want to do that, but then we also have an open route for people to come into this country who are professional staff". These comments came following a minimum estimated 38,000 nurse shortage;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clews |first=Graham |date=20 July 2022 |title=NHS facing 38,000 nurse shortage even if government hits recruitment target |url=https://www.nursingtimes.net/news/workforce/nhs-facing-38000-nurse-shortage-even-if-government-hits-recruitment-target-20-07-2022/ |access-date=15 October 2022 |website=Nursing Times |language=en |archive-date=15 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015153228/https://www.nursingtimes.net/news/workforce/nhs-facing-38000-nurse-shortage-even-if-government-hits-recruitment-target-20-07-2022/ |url-status=live}}</ref> the number of nurses leaving the NHS in London had risen by 24% the past year and more than two-thirds of [[NHS trust]]s were reporting a "significant or severe impact" from staff leaving for better paid jobs in retail and hospitality.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Keane |first=Daniel |date=12 October 2022 |title=Therese Coffey: Nurses don't need pay rise as Government 'has already helped' with cost of living |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/therese-coffey-nurses-dont-need-pay-rise-government-helped-cost-living-b1032055.html |access-date=15 October 2022 |work=Evening Standard |archive-date=14 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014210130/https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/therese-coffey-nurses-dont-need-pay-rise-government-helped-cost-living-b1032055.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 October 2022, it was reported Coffey was planning to allow people to obtain [[antibiotic]]s from [[pharmacist]]s without a prescription from a [[general practitioner]], which led to criticism by medical experts due to it increasing the risk of [[antimicrobial resistance]] (AMR).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smyth |first1=Chris |last2=Lay |first2=Kat |title=Chemists to prescribe antibiotics under Coffey health plan |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/healthcare/article/chemists-to-prescribe-antibiotics-under-coffey-health-plan-gjvfnb6q5 |access-date=15 October 2022 |date=15 October 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221015044359/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/chemists-to-prescribe-antibiotics-under-coffey-health-plan-gjvfnb6q5 |archive-date=15 October 2022 |language=en |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Doctors attack Thérèse Coffey's 'risky' plan for pharmacy antibiotic prescriptions without GPs |url=https://inews.co.uk/news/doctors-attack-therese-coffeys-risky-plan-for-pharmacy-antibiotic-prescriptions-without-gps-1914348 |access-date=16 October 2022 |work=inews.co.uk |date=15 October 2022 |language=en |archive-date=15 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015172601/https://inews.co.uk/news/doctors-attack-therese-coffeys-risky-plan-for-pharmacy-antibiotic-prescriptions-without-gps-1914348 |url-status=live}}</ref> At the same time, she received criticism for admitting to giving her own supply of antibiotics to others, which also increases the risk of AMR.<ref |language=en |archive-date=16 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016144015/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/oct/16/therese-coffey-criticised-for-giving-leftover-antibiotics-to-a-friend |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Lizzie |title=Therese Coffey admits handing out antibiotics to friends |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2022/10/15/therese-coffey-admits-handing-antibiotics-friends |access-date=16 October 2022 |work=The Telegraph |date=15 October 2022 |archive-date=15 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015231602/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2022/10/15/therese-coffey-admits-handing-antibiotics-friends/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rimi |first1=Aisha |title=Alarm over Coffey's 'plans to let patients get antibiotics without seeing GP' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/therese-coffey-plan-patients-antibiotics-gp-b2204363.html |access-date=18 October 2022 |work=The Independent |date=17 October 2022 |language=en |archive-date=18 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221018065546/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/therese-coffey-plan-patients-antibiotics-gp-b2204363.html |url-status=live}}</ref> This act – of sharing an antibiotics prescription with others – was also described as being illegal.<ref name="guardian-antibiotics"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=McCrum |first1=Sinead |title=Thérèse Coffey's alleged antibiotic habits seem seriously messed up |url=https://www.indy100.com/politics/therese-coffey-deputy-prime-minister-antibotics |access-date=18 October |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017172255/https://www.indy100.com/politics/therese-coffey-deputy-prime-minister-antibotics |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 October 2022,<ref name="poulter-opinion">{{cite news |last1=Poulter |first1=Dan |title=I'm a Tory MP, but I think Thérèse Coffey is putting ideology above the nation's health {{!}} Dan Poulter |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/oct/18/tory-mp-therese-coffey-health-secretary-smoking-obesity |access-date=20 October 2022 |work=the Guardian |date=18 October 2022 |language=en |archive-date=20 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020004433/http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/oct/18/tory-mp-therese-coffey-health-secretary-smoking-obesity |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Dan Poulter]] – a psychiatrist and former Conservative health minister – criticised Coffey's failure to tackle smoking and obesity, saying it leads to worse health and strains the NHS.<ref name="poulter-opinion"/><ref name="poulter-campbell">{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Denis |title=Coffey's 'ultra-libertarian' health stance risks lives, Tory ex-minister warns |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/oct/18/therese-coffey-ultra-libertarian-health-stance-risking-lives-tory-ex-minister-dan-poulter-warns |work=The Guardian |date=18 October 2022 |access-date=20 October 2022 |language=en |archive-date=19 October 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> After entering the House of Commons in 2010 Coffey repeatedly voted against measures to restrict smoking, including the ban on smoking in enclosed public spaces and the requirement that cigarettes be sold in plain packaging.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 October 2022 |title=Thérèse Coffey to drop smoking action plan, insiders say |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/oct/11/therese-coffey-to-drop-smoking-action-plan-insiders-say |access-date=13 October 2022 |work=The Guardian |archive-date=12 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012193358/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/oct/11/therese-coffey-to-drop-smoking-action-plan-insiders-say |url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2011, Coffey had accepted £1,100 in hospitality and gifts from [[Gallaher Group]] tobacco firm.<ref name="poulter-campbell"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Therese Coffey – TobaccoTactics |url=https://tobaccotactics.org/wiki/therese-coffey/ |access-date=23 April 2023 |website=tobaccotactics.org |language=en}}</ref>

=== Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs ===
Following [[Rishi Sunak]]'s appointment as prime minister, Coffey was retained in Sunak's cabinet and appointed [[Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|secretary of state for environment, food and rural affairs]] on 25 October 2022, but lost her position as deputy prime minister.<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 October 2022 |title=How green will new environment secretary Thérèse Coffey be? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/oct/26/how-green-will-new-environment-secretary-therese-coffey-be |access-date=26 October 2022 |work=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> She had previously held the positions of parliamentary under-secretary of state and minister of state for environment and rural opportunity within the [[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs]].

On 23 February 2023, Coffey was criticised for suggesting people [[Hunger in the United Kingdom|struggling to afford food]] could work for more hours to buy food, as well as suggesting that people eat turnips instead of tomatoes during [[2022–2023 food crises|a shortage of salad vegetables]] in the UK.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hassan |first1=Jennifer |title=Replace tomatoes with turnips? U.K. official's tip is root of new shortage. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2023/02/26/therese-coffey-uk-tomato-salad-shortage-turnips/ |access-date=16 March 2023 |newspaper=Washington Post |date=26 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Zoe |title=Environment secretary urges Britons to 'cherish' turnips amid food shortages |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/feb/23/food-shortages-environment-secretary-urges-britons-cherish-turnips |access-date=16 March 2023 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=23 February 2023}}</ref> [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] MP [[Rachael Maskell]] said, "It's very shocking that the Environment Secretary shifted blame for food poverty onto people because they are on low wages and are poor." Coffey acknowledged that inflation was "really tough at the moment" and that support schemes were in place.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eat turnips during vegetable shortage, suggests Therese Coffey |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-64745258 |access-date=16 March 2023 |work=[[BBC News Online|BBC News]] |date=23 February 2023}}</ref>

[[File:The Prime Minister reshuffles his cabinet (53329850453).jpg|thumb|Coffey in Downing Street, with [[Larry the Cat|Larry the cat]], on her way to submit her resignation on 13 November 2023]]
She resigned from the role on 13 November 2023 during a [[Sunak ministry#November 2023 – present|cabinet reshuffle]], stating "I consider it is now the right time to step back from government".<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 November 2023 |title=British environment minister Coffey resigns in reshuffle |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/british-environment-minister-coffey-quits-2023-11-13/ |access-date=13 November 2023}}</ref> In a [[BBC Radio]] interview on 15 November, Coffey cited [[Occupational burnout|work-related stress]] as a reason for her resignation, stating that she had "nearly died" after becoming ill because of the stress of being a minister five years previously.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-suffolk-67415285|title=Suffolk MP Therese Coffey says she nearly died due to stress|last1=Eustace|first1=Shannon|last2=Santos|first2=Joao|date=15 November 2023|work=[[BBC News]]|accessdate=16 November 2023}}</ref>

At the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|general election on 4 July 2024]], Coffey lost her seat in parliament.<ref name="auto"/>

=== House of Lords ===
Coffey was nominated for a [[life peer]]age by Conservative leader [[Kemi Badenoch]] in late 2024.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=20 December 2024 |title=Political Peerages December 2024 |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/political-peerages-december-2024 |website=[[GOV.UK]] |publisher=[[Prime Minister's Office (United Kingdom)|Prime Minister's Office, 10 Downing Street]] |access-date=20 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pollock |first=Laura |date=20 December 2024 |title=See the 38 new lifetime peers announced by the UK Government |url=https://www.thenational.scot/news/24808667.see-new-lifetime-peers-announced-uk-government/ |work=[[The National (Scotland)|The National]] |access-date=20 December 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241220145456/https://www.thenational.scot/news/24808667.see-new-lifetime-peers-announced-uk-government/ |archive-date=20 December 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> She was created ''Baroness Coffey, of Saxmundham in the County of Suffolk and of Grassendale in the City of Liverpool'', on 17 January 2025,<ref>{{London Gazette |date=22 January 2025 |issue=64638 |page=1070}}</ref> and was [[Introduction (House of Lords)|introduced to the House of Lords]] on 21 January.<ref>{{Cite Hansard |title=Introduction: Baroness Coffey |url=https://hansard.parliament.uk/lords/2025-01-21/debates/4F8BF2EA-65CE-4D99-B4A3-112C50B832AC/IntroductionBaronessCoffey |date=21 January 2025 |jurisdiction=Parliament of the United Kingdom |house=House of Lords |volume=842 |column=1577}}</ref>

In September 2026, in the House of Lords, Coffey said that the "pension triple lock" should be reviewed and that it should "probably" be scrapped and changed into a "double lock" or different system.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/money/general/state-pension-triple-lock-position-confirmed-as-should-be-replaced/ar-AA2bz9GL?ocid=edgntpruby&pc=ASTS&cvid=6a9ae1c6d2554c4aa0f4282f023f8e92&uxmode=ruby&ei=13 |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Coffey is single and is described as a private person.<ref name="Tip for chief whip"/> Coffey employed her sister Clare as a secretary in her parliamentary office starting in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm/cmregmem/200302/200302.pdf |page=97 |title=Register of Members' Financial Interests as at 2 March 2020 |access-date=10 March 2020 |work=UK Parliament |archive-date=21 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200321053022/https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm/cmregmem/200302/200302.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>

Coffey is an avid football fan, supporting [[Liverpool Football Club]]. She signed an [[early day motion]] in 2011, set down by Labour [[Liverpool Walton]] MP [[Steve Rotheram]], requesting a [[Knight Bachelor|knighthood]] for [[Kenny Dalglish]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-13206349 |title=Commons call for Kenny Dalglish knighthood |work=BBC News |date=27 April 2011 |access-date=27 April 2011 |archive-date=29 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110429035643/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-13206349 |url-status=live }}</ref> She enjoys gardening, karaoke, and music.<ref name=":0" />

In an interview with ''[[The Sunday Times]]'', Coffey said she spent a month in hospital in 2018 after the stress of being a government minister led to a [[brain abscess]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Rachel |title=Therese Coffey: Brain abscess from stress left me 'close to dying' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-67606077 |work=BBC News |date=3 December 2023}}</ref>

==Honours==
On 4 July 2024, Coffey was appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) in the [[2024 Dissolution Honours]] for political and public service.<ref>{{London Gazette |date=7 August 2024 |issue=64480 |page=15222 |supp=y}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=Dissolution Honours 2024 |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dissolution-honours-2024 |website=GOV.UK |language=en |date=4 July 2024 |access-date=4 July 2024}}</ref>
